chat.emptyDescription: See how demand, menu, and hours look right now — or switch to Image assistant to create images.

locationOverview.label: Location overview
locationOverview.prompt: Start with a general description of this location: name, cuisine, address, and opening hours. Then summarize the current situation from sales charts when available: strong and weak day × meal-period demand, which dishes to feature (evergreen vs daily highlights vs day specialties), and interesting menu combos. End with at most two practical next steps. Use a short markdown brief (Demand, Menu, Combos, Hours, Next). Do not build a weekly Instagram schedule unless I ask.

weeklyPlan.label: Weekly Instagram plan
weeklyPlan.prompt: Create a weekly Instagram plan for this venue. First load location opening hours, then present the plan with the weekly schedule tool (one entry per posting slot). Prefer open days and posting times during or shortly before service. For each slot include a suggested posting time, the format (Story, post, carousel, or Reel), the menu items to feature, a short caption angle, and a one-line why based on open hours and sales or demand when available.

featureTopDishes.label: Feature top dishes
featureTopDishes.prompt: From this location’s current menu performance, which dishes should we feature and why? Mention timing (day or meal period) when the charts support it, and keep Instagram as optional — not a full week plan.

storiesAndReels.label: Stories & Reels mix
storiesAndReels.prompt: Draft a weekly mix of Instagram Stories and Reels with specific menu items for each slot and a brief creative direction.

milestonePreset.dialogDescription: Choose a template to prefill the milestone, or start empty.

dates.label: Dates
dates.title: Dates
dates.summary: Set the campaign date window and list public holidays for this location.
dates.goal: Resolve the campaign date window and list public holidays between startDate and endDate for this location.
dates.criterionStartDate: **startDate** is present in the data and matches the selected input window.
dates.criterionEndDate: **endDate** is present in the data and matches the selected input window.
dates.criterionPublicHolidays: **publicHolidays** is present for the selected date window (an empty list is valid when no holidays fall in range).

promotion_candidates.label: Promotion candidates
promotion_candidates.title: Promotion candidates
promotion_candidates.summary: Surface star and puzzle menu items by category from promotion-engineering signals.
promotion_candidates.inputDescription: Optional orientation notes for storytelling emphasis. Checked menu categories above scope which POS sections appear in results; leave all selected to include every category. List menu item names to exclude (one per line) in the ignored-items field.
promotion_candidates.inputPlaceholder: e.g. prioritize family bundles and lunch heroes this month…
promotion_candidates.goal: Fetch promotion-engineering candidates and present star and puzzle menu items by POS menu category. Use the Campaign Brief top-revenue POS category as campaign focus and list that category first in the preview.
promotion_candidates.criterionCategoriesPresent: Data includes at least one menu category section with **starItems** and/or **puzzleItems** when analytics return candidates for the selected categories.
promotion_candidates.criterionItemsOnlyFromSignals: **starItems** and **puzzleItems** only include menu names from promotion-engineering signals (no invented items).

menu_tagger.label: Menu tagger
menu_tagger.title: Menu tagger
menu_tagger.summary: Tag promotion candidates with a fixed taxonomy for culinary and reel-oriented dimensions.
menu_tagger.inputDescription: Optional guidance for ambiguous dishes. The run reads prior Promotion Candidates milestone data and assigns fixed taxonomy tags to each star and puzzle item.
menu_tagger.inputPlaceholder: e.g. treat bubble tea as drink; map regional dish names to rice vs noodle…
menu_tagger.goal: Read saved Promotion Candidates from an earlier workflow milestone and attach fixed taxonomy v2 tags (culinary dimensions plus reel-oriented dimensions such as reel moment, texture, prep style, occasion, serve temp, and content angle) to every star and puzzle menu item. Place this milestone after Promotion Candidates in the timeline.
menu_tagger.criterionPriorPromotionCandidates: Run used a prior **promotion_candidates** milestone with at least one star or puzzle item.
menu_tagger.criterionAllItemsTagged: Every promotion candidate item has required single-value tags (**kind**, **reel_moment**, **serve_temp**) and optional multi-value dimension arrays.
menu_tagger.criterionTaxonomyOnly: All tag values come from the fixed **v2 taxonomy** enums (no free-form tags). Empty optional tag arrays are valid.

menu_clusterer.label: Menu clusterer
menu_clusterer.title: Menu clusterer
menu_clusterer.summary: Group tagged menu items into categorical and creative clusters plus top-five lists.
menu_clusterer.targetGroupCountDescription: Optional. Leave empty to derive from tagged menu size (4–12 clusters, ~4 items per cluster). Set a value between 4 and 12 for more granular groupings on large menus.
menu_clusterer.inputDescription: Optional guidance for cluster emphasis. The run reads prior Campaign Brief and Menu Tagger data, builds one deterministic Top 5 group per POS category that has star items, then uses AI to create menu clusters from menu tagger tags plus campaign brief strategy.
menu_clusterer.inputPlaceholder: e.g. prioritize signature mains with the highest sales, or split snacks and drinks into separate clusters…
menu_clusterer.goal: Read prior Campaign Brief strategy plus **tagged menu items** from Menu Tagger. Build one **top_five** group per available POS category that has **star** items (carousel posts). Then generate **menu clusters** (4–12, sized from the tagged menu or milestone input) entirely via AI: **categorical** clusters from shared POS category and tag signals, and **creative** cross-category clusters (e.g. snacks with hot drinks) aligned with the campaign brief. Every tagged item must appear in at least one cluster.
menu_clusterer.criterionPriorCampaignBrief: Run used a prior **restaurant_campaign_brief** milestone with saved strategy data.
menu_clusterer.criterionPriorMenuTagger: Run used a prior **menu_tagger** milestone with tagged items.
menu_clusterer.criterionHookGroupCount: Data includes the derived or configured number of **menu clusters** (4–12) and one **top five group per available category** that has star items.
menu_clusterer.criterionCategoryScope: When the tagged menu spans multiple POS categories, menu clusters include both **categorical** (same POS category, grounded in menu tagger tags) and **creative** (cross-category) groups.
menu_clusterer.criterionTopFiveLead: Each menu cluster's position-1 item is in the **top popularity score-tier** (top five scores; storytelling breaks ties among same score). Each top five group's position-1 item is the **top star** in that category by popularity.
menu_clusterer.criterionClusterDescription: Each cluster includes a **clusterDescription** explaining grouping rationale and location-concept fit.

scheduler.label: Scheduler
scheduler.title: Scheduler
scheduler.summary: Place feed posts, Stories, and Reels on the calendar within the campaign window.
scheduler.inputDescription: Optional guidance for scheduling emphasis. This step reads the campaign window from **dates** and business strategy from **restaurant_campaign_brief**.
scheduler.inputPlaceholder: e.g. prioritize weekday lunch reels and holiday stories on public holidays from dates…
scheduler.goal: Read the campaign window from **dates** and business strategy from **restaurant_campaign_brief**, then place feed posts, Stories, and Reels on the calendar as title-only slots with explicit **kind**, **date**, and **time** within the campaign window.
scheduler.criterionDatesWindow: Scheduler data includes **startDate** and **endDate** from the prior **dates** milestone.
scheduler.criterionSlotsInWindow: All scheduled slot **dates** fall within the campaign window.
scheduler.criterionCampaignBriefContext: Scheduler used prior **restaurant_campaign_brief** strategy for timing and cadence.
scheduler.criterionAtLeastOneSlot: Scheduler includes at least one scheduled slot.

culture_hooks.label: Culture hooks
culture_hooks.title: Culture hooks
culture_hooks.summary: Find non-food heritage and place topics that resonate with the local audience.
culture_hooks.inputDescription: Optional direction for tone and emphasis. The run uses prior Campaign Brief data to infer heritage/origin places and topics the local audience would find interesting (non-food, non-drink).
culture_hooks.inputPlaceholder: e.g. prioritize Italian coastal towns and family travel nostalgia…
culture_hooks.goal: Use Campaign Brief data to infer the restaurant's concept/origin geography and the venue's local target audience, then list 3–5 non-food, non-drink heritage/place topics (regions, landmarks, place-tied rituals) that the audience would find interesting or share affinity with. These topics should inspire Instagram feed posts, Stories, and Reels that attract potential new customers.
culture_hooks.criterionIntersectionsPresent: Data includes **3-5 non-food intersections** with concrete topic, concept link, audience relevance, and content example suitable for a feed post, Story, or Reel. Prefer heritage/origin place topics when origin is inferable.
culture_hooks.criterionNonFood: Intersections are **not food- or drink-centric** (no dishes, coffee, beverages, recipes, or flavor-led angles).
culture_hooks.criterionAudienceConceptInferred: Data clearly states **locationConcept** (concept and inferred origin geography when available) and **targetAudience**, both inferred from Campaign Brief context.

ig_profile.label: IG Profile
ig_profile.title: IG Profile
ig_profile.summary: Suggest Instagram usernames and bio variations from the campaign brief.
ig_profile.inputDescription: Optional direction for username style and bio emphasis. The run uses only prior Campaign Brief data to generate Instagram profile suggestions.
ig_profile.inputPlaceholder: e.g. prefer short handles; emphasize reservations and lunch service…
ig_profile.goal: Read Campaign Brief data and generate Instagram profile suggestions — username options and three bio variations — aligned with brand, audience, and campaign objective.
ig_profile.criterionUsernames: Data includes **3–5 username suggestions** in valid Instagram format, each with a one-line rationale.
ig_profile.criterionBioLength: Each **bio variation** text is at most **150 characters** (Instagram hard limit).
ig_profile.criterionBioBreakdown: Each bio variation breakdown covers **hook**, **value prop**, **CTA**, and **tone**, grounded in Campaign Brief context.
ig_profile.criterionBioVariations: Data includes **3 distinct bio variations** in the bios array.

ig_plan.label: IG Plan
ig_plan.title: IG Plan
ig_plan.summary: Build a weekly Instagram slot strategy from the brief and venue demand signals.
ig_plan.inputDescription: Optional guidance for weekly cadence or marketing emphasis. Requires a prior **Campaign Brief** milestone with saved data. The run also fetches venue slot demand signals and menu engineering portfolio distribution from the workflow-pinned analytics run.
ig_plan.inputPlaceholder: e.g. push afternoon traffic Wed–Fri; protect Friday dinner…
ig_plan.goal: Read prior **Campaign Brief** strategy (objectives, pillars, cadence, audience) together with venue slot demand signals and menu engineering portfolio distribution from the workflow-pinned analytics run, then output a **weekly slot strategy grid** in `entries[]`. Each entry defines publish **day** and **slot** (HH:MM), marketing **objective**, content **pillar**, target **mealPeriod**, **slotStrategy** (`maintain`, `support`, `grow`, or `aggressively_grow`), and **productRole** (`star`, `puzzle`, or `plow_horse`). Classify slots from analytics; ground objectives and pillar mix in the campaign brief. Strategy only; no dish names, hooks, captions, or format assignments.
ig_plan.criterionWeeklyEntries: Data includes a non-empty **entries** array. Each row has **day**, **slot** (HH:MM), **objective**, **pillar**, **mealPeriod**, **productRole**, **slotStrategy**, and **slotKey**. Rows are grouped in weekday order (monday through sunday).
ig_plan.criterionSlotGrounding: Each entry uses a valid **slotStrategy** (`maintain`, `support`, `grow`, or `aggressively_grow`), **pillar**, and **productRole** (`star`, `puzzle`, or `plow_horse`). Publish **slot** times should be plausible for the venue day when opening hours are available.
ig_plan.criterionScheduleExplanation: Data includes a non-empty **scheduleExplanation** summarizing the weekly marketing allocation strategy.
ig_plan.criterionCampaignBriefAlignment: The weekly plan reflects prior **Campaign Brief** strategy, content pillars, and cadence guidance — objectives and pillar mix align with the brief without contradicting analytics-based slot classification.

ig_menu_picker.label: IG Menu Picker
ig_menu_picker.title: IG Menu Picker
ig_menu_picker.summary: Attach 1–3 menu items to each selected IG Plan slot with a short rationale.
ig_menu_picker.inputDescription: Select which IG Plan slots to process and add optional guidance for menu emphasis. The run uses the workflow-pinned sales report for slot menu candidates.
ig_menu_picker.inputPlaceholder: e.g. favor vegetarian stars for weekday lunch slots…
ig_menu_picker.goal: Read prior **IG Plan** milestone data, filter by selected slots, fetch menu engineering and per-slot candidates from the workflow-pinned analytics run, then attach **1–3 menu items** per selected entry with a short rationale.
ig_menu_picker.criterionPriorIgPlan: A prior **ig_plan** milestone with saved **entries** exists earlier in the workflow.
ig_menu_picker.criterionMenuItemsPerEntry: Each selected entry in the output has **1–3 menuItems** with non-empty **menu** names.
ig_menu_picker.criterionSelectedEntriesOnly: Output **entries** include only slots selected on the Input tab (empty selection = all IG Plan entries).

ig_format.label: IG Format
ig_format.title: IG Format
ig_format.summary: Assign reel, post, carousel, or story formats to menu-picker slots.
ig_format.inputDescription: Optional guidance for format emphasis. Menu picker entries are read-only — the run assigns a format to every prior slot with menu items.
ig_format.inputPlaceholder: e.g. favor reels for aggressively_grow slots; use carousels for multi-dish discovery…
ig_format.goal: Read prior **IG Menu Picker** milestone data and assign an Instagram **format** (`reel`, `post`, `post-carousel`, or `story`) to each entry with menu items, preserving plan strategy and dish selections.
ig_format.criterionPriorIgMenuPicker: A prior **ig_menu_picker** milestone with saved **entries** that include **menuItems** exists earlier in the workflow.
ig_format.criterionValidType: Each output entry has a valid **type** (`reel`, `post`, `post-carousel`, or `story`) and non-empty **formatRationale**.
ig_format.criterionSlotCoverage: Output **entries** slot coverage matches the prior menu picker (same slotKeys, no extras or omissions).
ig_format.criterionCarouselMenuItems: **post-carousel** is used only when an entry has **2+ menuItems**.

ig_text.label: IG Text
ig_text.title: IG Text
ig_text.summary: Generate Instagram copy fields for each formatted slot from the campaign brief.
ig_text.inputDescription: Optional guidance for copy tone and emphasis. IG Format entries are read-only — the run generates text fields per slot using Campaign Brief orientation.
ig_text.inputPlaceholder: e.g. keep headlines short in Bahasa Indonesia; playful tone for weekend slots…
ig_text.goal: Read prior **IG Format** milestone data and **Campaign Brief** orientation, then generate Instagram **texts** (`field` + `value`) per slot while preserving plan strategy, dishes, and format assignments.
ig_text.criterionPriorIgFormat: A prior **ig_format** milestone with saved **entries** that include **type** and **menuItems** exists earlier in the workflow.
ig_text.criterionSlotCoverage: Output **entries** slot coverage matches the prior IG Format (same slotKeys, no extras or omissions).
ig_text.criterionNonemptyTexts: Every output entry has a non-empty **texts** array with non-empty **field** and **value** pairs.
ig_text.criterionRequiredFields: Each entry includes all required text **fields** for its format **type** (post, reel, story, or post-carousel with indexed slide fields).
ig_text.criterionCampaignBriefAlignment: Generated copy aligns with **Campaign Brief** tone, messaging, and guardrails used as orientation.

restaurant_campaign_brief.label: Campaign brief
restaurant_campaign_brief.title: Campaign brief
restaurant_campaign_brief.summary: Build a campaign brief with strategy, audience, messaging, and measurement guardrails.
restaurant_campaign_brief.inputDescription: Optional context for generation (style, positioning, constraints). Example: during a soccer World Cup period, note campaign priorities or tone for match days. Included with location and analytics data when you run or generate the brief.
restaurant_campaign_brief.inputPlaceholder: e.g. Family-friendly trattoria tone; highlight lunch and vegetarian options…
restaurant_campaign_brief.reflectionDescription: When enabled, a quality pass reviews the draft against your pass criteria and revises weak sections before the brief is saved. Milestone evaluation still runs afterward to verify completeness.
restaurant_campaign_brief.goal: The data holds a factual campaign brief foundation: venue snapshot, an explicit overall business strategy for audience ordering and lunch-first focus, objective and funnel stage, target segments, message hierarchy, CTA/offer plan, content and proof strategy, plus measurement/testing/risk guardrails grounded in available analytics.
restaurant_campaign_brief.criterionStartDate: **startDate** is set in the data using the Input tab campaign window.
restaurant_campaign_brief.criterionEndDate: **endDate** is set in the data using the Input tab campaign window.
restaurant_campaign_brief.criterionPublicHolidays: **publicHolidays** is generated for the campaign window and listed in the data.
restaurant_campaign_brief.criterionVenueSnapshot: **Venue snapshot** in the data names the venue and uses city/country/currency when known; it does not invent full addresses.
restaurant_campaign_brief.criterionOverallStrategy: **Overall strategy** names a primary focus, ordered audience priority, reusable core message, offer window, and cadence guidance that downstream scheduling can follow.
restaurant_campaign_brief.criterionContentPillars: **Content pillars** include 3-5 unique non-empty items that are concrete enough to guide campaign content.
restaurant_campaign_brief.criterionAudienceHypotheses: **Audience hypotheses** include 3-5 unique non-empty items that are plausible for the venue context and usable for campaign planning. They should align with available data signals when present, but exact signal keywords or strict demographic proof in every line are optional. Fail only when items are empty, duplicated, or clearly disconnected from context.
restaurant_campaign_brief.criterionProofAngles: **Proof-oriented angles** include 3-5 unique non-empty items and are concrete, evidence-oriented reasons to believe the campaign message. They should align with known venue/menu context when available; naming exact menu items or category labels in every line is optional.
restaurant_campaign_brief.criterionToneGuardrails: **Tone guardrails** include 3-5 unique non-empty items that are coherent with venue context and provide usable writing constraints.
restaurant_campaign_brief.criterionCampaignObjective: **Campaign objective** states one primary business outcome and a dominant funnel stage. Equivalent stage phrasing is acceptable.
restaurant_campaign_brief.criterionTargetSegments: **Target segments** include 3-5 unique non-empty items that are actionable for campaign planning. Pass when segments are clear and usable; strict taxonomy is optional.
restaurant_campaign_brief.criterionMessageHierarchy: **Message hierarchy** includes 3-5 unique lines with a clear priority order for promise, proof, and call-to-action across the set. Exact wording in each line is flexible.
restaurant_campaign_brief.criterionOfferAndCtaPlan: **Offer and CTA plan** includes 3-5 unique lines that explain realistic guest actions and margin-safe offer framing. Not every line needs every channel.
restaurant_campaign_brief.criterionContentPillarPlan: **Content pillar plan** includes 3-5 unique lines mapping pillars to executable campaign guidance (such as angle, format, or CTA emphasis). Rigid templates are optional.
restaurant_campaign_brief.criterionMeasurementPlan: **Measurement plan** includes 3-5 unique lines with clear metrics and practical decision signals. Exact threshold phrasing is optional if decision intent is clear.
restaurant_campaign_brief.criterionTestingPlan: **Testing plan** includes 3-5 unique lines with concrete experiments and follow-up actions when performance is weak. Exact test taxonomy is optional.
restaurant_campaign_brief.criterionRiskGuardrails: **Risk guardrails** include 3-5 unique lines covering brand, regulatory, or operational constraints and clear avoidances where relevant.

chat.milestoneCampaignBriefInputDescription: Optional context for generation (style, positioning, constraints). Example: during a soccer World Cup period, note campaign priorities or tone for match days. Included with location and analytics data when you run or generate the brief.

chat.milestoneCampaignBriefPreviewHelpVenueSn: The venue snapshot names where you operate (city, country, currency) so Instagram geotags, local collaborations, and “visit us” language stay accurate—not invented addresses.
chat.milestoneCampaignBriefPreviewHelpOverall: The overall strategy turns the brief into something schedulable: it records the main business focus, who should be prioritized first, the reusable core message, the offer window, and cadence guidance that downstream Reel planning can follow.
chat.milestoneCampaignBriefPreviewHelpContent: Content pillars are recurring themes for your feed (for example brunch, chef favorites, or weekday lunch). They keep Stories and Reels coherent so you rotate angles without random one-off topics.
chat.milestoneCampaignBriefPreviewHelpAudienc: Audience hypotheses describe who you expect to reach and when, grounded in your data. They guide posting times, tone, and creative hooks so Instagram content matches real behavior, not generic demographics alone.
chat.milestoneCampaignBriefPreviewHelpProofOr: Proof-oriented angles are evidence-backed reasons to believe you (dishes, operations, social proof). They make captions and Reels credible and specific—stronger than generic “best in town” claims.
chat.milestoneCampaignBriefPreviewHelpToneGua: Tone guardrails define voice and boundaries for Instagram copy, replies, and community management so messaging stays on-brand and avoids mismatched humor or claims.
chat.milestoneCampaignBriefPreviewHelpCampaig: The campaign objective states what success looks like (for example awareness vs bookings). It aligns CTAs, offers, and what you optimize for in Instagram analytics.
chat.milestoneCampaignBriefPreviewHelpTargetS: Target segments are moment-based clusters (for example weekday lunch vs weekend families). They let you tailor hooks and formats to when those audiences actually scroll.
chat.milestoneCampaignBriefPreviewHelpMessage: Message hierarchy orders your lead promise, proof, and call-to-action. It keeps single-image posts and short Reels legible so viewers know what to do after three seconds.
chat.milestoneCampaignBriefPreviewHelpOfferAn: The offer and CTA plan ties asks (reserve, DM, order, walk-in) to constraints that protect margin. It prevents Instagram promos from promising what ops cannot honor.
chat.milestoneCampaignBriefPreviewHelpContent: The content pillar plan maps each pillar to objective, format bias, and CTA role so scheduling balances Reels, carousels, and Stories across the campaign—not only one content type.
chat.milestoneCampaignBriefPreviewHelpMeasure: The measurement plan lists what to watch weekly or monthly on Instagram (and related signals) so you know whether the brief is working before the campaign ends.
chat.milestoneCampaignBriefPreviewHelpTesting: The testing plan defines what to try by daypart, day of week, or format—and what to change if results lag—so learning is explicit, not accidental A/B on the fly.
chat.milestoneCampaignBriefPreviewHelpRiskGua: Risk guardrails cover brand, regulatory, and operational limits plus topics or visuals to avoid—critical for alcohol, health claims, minors, and licensed imagery on a public channel.
chat.milestoneCampaignBriefPreviewHelpStartDa: Start date anchors when campaign messaging and scheduling begin—used for countdown posts, holiday overlap, and aligning promotion candidates and the scheduler.
chat.milestoneCampaignBriefPreviewHelpEndDate: End date marks when offers or campaign-specific messaging should stop so Instagram posts do not advertise expired deals or past windows.
chat.milestoneCampaignBriefPreviewHelpPublicH: Public holidays in the campaign window help you plan timely posts (hours, specials, cultural moments) and avoid surprises when the kitchen or traffic pattern shifts.
chat.milestonePromotionCandidatesPreviewSumma: Star items sell well; puzzle items sell less but may have margin or story upside. Use this list to decide what to feature, discount, or reframe on Instagram.
chat.milestonePromotionCandidatesPreviewHelpH: Promotion candidates come from menu engineering on your sales data. They are grouped by menu category so you can brief the kitchen and marketing on the same shortlist.
chat.milestonePromotionCandidatesPreviewHelpS: Star items are high performers on the menu. They are safe anchors for promos and hero posts because guests already choose them often.
chat.milestonePromotionCandidatesPreviewHelpP: Puzzle items are not top sellers yet. They may deserve better photos, bundling, or storytelling—or a gentle nudge off the menu if they tie up the line.
chat.milestonePromotionCandidatesPreviewHelpS: Storytelling fit estimates how easy it is to make an authentic Instagram story around a dish—local ingredients, craft, ritual, or culture—not just food styling.
chat.milestonePromotionCandidatesPreviewQuant: {count, plural, one {# unit sold} other {# units sold}}
chat.milestonePromotionCandidatesPreviewHelpP: Popularity is the share of units sold within this menu category bucket (or the full menu when categories are missing). Higher means guests order that dish more often relative to other items in the same bucket.

Price level ranks each dish within its menu category by average selling price: low (bottom third), mid (middle third), or high (top third). It helps you balance premium hero dishes with accessible entry points in the same promo set.

chat.milestoneMenuClustererPreviewHelpUnassig: Menu tagger items that were not placed in any food cluster.
chat.milestoneMenuTaggerPreviewHelpUsedTags: Unique tags rolled up across all tagged menu items, grouped by taxonomy dimension. Use this to see which ingredients, reel moments, and content angles appear in your lineup.
chat.milestoneMenuTaggerPreviewHelpTaggedItem: Each dish from promotion candidates with AI-assigned tags. Star and puzzle badges reflect menu-engineering roles from analytics; the storytelling badge shows how well the dish name fits your campaign brief for Instagram content.
chat.milestoneMenuTaggerPreviewHelp_reel_mome: The visual beat to capture on camera for Reels — steam, sizzle, pour, stretch, and similar moments that stop the scroll.
chat.milestoneMenuTaggerPreviewHelp_content_a: How to frame the dish in content — signature hero, hidden gem, behind-the-scenes, or similar editorial angle.
chat.milestoneMenuTaggerPreviewHelp_texture: Mouthfeel cues for captions and shot direction — crispy, creamy, juicy, and similar texture tags.
chat.milestoneMenuTaggerPreviewHelp_prep_styl: How the dish is made — grilled, fried, baked, raw, and similar prep cues for kitchen or process content.
